eval.title: Buffett Keeps Buying Occidental Stock + Oil Price Outlook!

call.headline_quote: it has not yet triggered the okay now we can start with a position

base_metric.name: fcf_per_share
base_metric.quote: I have put in a 100% payout ratio as they could be paying let's say all the free cash flow they are getting now per share in dividends

scenarios.name: normal
scenarios.quote: the free cash flows grow at just 4% % discount rate 10% terminal multiple on the free cash flows 10 then the intrinsic value is 51 per share which is close to where we are now

reasons.claim: Thin margins mean a small drop in oil prices wipes out most of the profit, making the stock highly volatile with oil.
reasons.quote: just a small 10% decline in oil prices all else equal there is not much profit left this means that the margins are thin which means when oil prices go up accidental stock shoots up when oil prices go lower accidental has issues

reasons.claim: Below roughly $60 oil, Occidental generates no free cash flow, creating survival risk and making valuation impossible in that scenario.
reasons.quote: if oil prices go to below 60 there is no free cash flow for accidental then there is surviving and then you cannot value it

data_check.gap_note: he says 260, as-of 1.1439e+10 (FY2024); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: Management is paying down debt from the Crown Rock acquisition, which lowers interest payments and should allow higher dividends.
reasons.quote: their target is 15 billion of debt that's 10 billion down that is 33% of less interest payments that would then push the dividend higher

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: debt target

reasons.claim: Berkshire's large ownership gives Occidental effectively unlimited access to capital, letting it survive downturns.
reasons.quote: because if birkshire owns 30% of the company it has unlimited access to Capital thus it can survive whatever

data_check.gap_note: trajectory visible at T0; no number stated

reasons.claim: At current 10% free cash flow yield the stock has not yet reached the margin of safety he requires versus his existing 15-position portfolio.
reasons.quote: Occidental now gives me 10% free cash flow yield perhaps a little bit lower and I have already 15 positions there looking in some other things so it has not yet triggered

external_facts_used: Warren Buffett/Berkshire Hathaway's continued buying and ~30% ownership stake in Occidental
Short-term Energy Outlook forecasts for oil supply/demand and prices
IEA World Energy Outlook scenarios (STEPS, Announced Pledges, Net Zero)
Conference call commentary on debt paydown targets and Gulf of Mexico/Gulf of America naming

critic.notes: He values it at IV ~51 near price (~10% return), says viewers can start a 3% position now and it's a 'rare exception' to make money, though he personally waits for a margin of safety. That is fair_hold, not avoid.
